title: Configuration Studio: one frame of a run, the body of a run.frame event and an element of a wait=true response (ADR-A154)

run.description: The run's IRI, urn:lattice:studio:run: and a lower-case UUID

seq.description: The frame's place in the run, from 0. A run sends at most 128 frames, so a worker's frames end at 127. The service's own failed frame at the deadline comes one past the last it forwarded, which may be 128

last.description: True on the run's final frame and on no other

part.description: The part this frame's text belongs to, given on the first frame of each part only

index.description: The part's place in the run. Parts are counted from 0 with no gap

role.description: What the part is. report and artefact are defined by the contract. check, request, delta and outcome are the four parts of a simulator step, defined by the slices that build the simulators

mediaType.description: The media type of the part's text, for example text/turtle

path.description: The artefact's relative path, with / separators, as cst:path gives it

group.description: What the part belongs to, such as the mapping an artefact was written by, as cst:group gives it

step.description: The step of the run that wrote the part, from 0, as cst:stratum gives it for a mapping dry run

text.description: A piece of the current part's text. A part's text is the concatenation of the text of its frames in sequence order. At most 49,152 bytes as UTF-8 and never split inside a character, which a schema states only as 49,152 characters, so the worker holds the byte rule

more.description: A hint that the current part continues in the next frame, so that a display can say more of it is coming. A frame with no part continues the current part whatever the frame before it said, and a client must not rely on more

status.description: On the last frame only. A failed last frame settles the run whatever is missing before it, and a run is complete only when its last frame succeeded and every frame from 0 to it is present

message.description: Why the run failed, in plain words. On a last frame whose status is failed. Such a frame settles the run as failed, whatever frames before it are missing

conforms.description: Whether what the run checked conforms. On a last frame whose status is succeeded
